jobs.descriptionHtml:
Location: Onsite — Austin, TX

Employment Type: Direct Hire, Full‑Time

Job Title: Perception Engineer

About 9 Mothers

The modern battlefield has changed. Cheap, autonomous suicide drones have turned the tactical advantage upside down, and the world is looking for a solution. At 9 Mothers, we aren’t just "innovating"—we are building the shield.

Backed by top-tier investors, we develop AI powered machines designed to intercept and neutralize Group 1/sUAS threats in real-time. Our flagship product is a low-power, counter-drone system built for the edge—on vehicles, at bases, or in a soldier's pack.

Why 9 Mothers?

While others build for "awareness" or "long-term research," we build for the immediate survival of those in harm’s way. We are a team of hackers, engineers, and mission-driven builders who value field-ready capability over polished slide decks. If you want to see your code or hardware in the field next month—not next year—this is your playground.

Position Summary

9 Mothers is seeking a Perception Engineer to own the computer vision and machine learning stack that powers target detection, classification, and tracking in our counter-sUAS systems. The Perception Lead is responsible for the research, development, and deployment of the perception pipeline that enables EDDA to engage aerial threats in real time. This is a senior individual contributor position.

Essential Duties

  • Own the visual perception pipeline end-to-end, including detection, classification, and tracking of sUAS targets in real time.

  • Design and train machine learning models that meet latency and accuracy requirements for edge deployment on Jetson-class hardware.

  • Architect and maintain the dataset and simulation pipeline, including data collection, labeling, curation, augmentation, synthetic data generation, and closed-loop retraining based on field performance.

  • Optimize inference performance on Jetson platforms, including model pruning, quantization, TensorRT integration, and custom kernel development as required.

  • Establish the model evaluation framework and metrics used to assess perception performance under operational conditions.

  • Deliver target state information (position, velocity, identity, uncertainty) to the controls subsystem.

  • Collaborate with the hardware team on camera, optics, and sensor selection.

Requirements

  • 6+ years of professional experience in computer vision or machine learning, including production deployment on edge hardware.

  • Demonstrated experience shipping a detection or tracking system under real-world latency, small-object, or adversarial constraints.

  • Strong engineering skills beyond modeling, including experience with PyTorch or JAX through to deployed, optimized inference.

  • Proficiency in Python for model development and C++ or Rust for deployed inference.

  • U.S. citizenship and ability to pass a background check.

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience working with infrared (IR), thermal, or multi-spectrum camera systems.

  • TensorRT and NVIDIA Jetson deployment experience at production scale.

  • Multi-object tracking under challenging conditions.

  • Multi-modal sensor fusion experience (EO/IR, radar, acoustic).

  • Synthetic data generation and sim-to-real methodologies.

  • Prior experience in defense or other safety-critical computer vision applications.

  • Active security clearance, or eligibility to obtain one.

  • A passion for building robots or engineering projects as a hobby.

Benefits

  • Meaningful Early Equity: You aren't just an employee; you are a foundational owner. Your contributions directly drive the value of your stake in the company.

  • Direct Roadmap Influence: Forget the bureaucracy of big defense. You will have a seat at the table, directly shaping our product and technology trajectory from day one.

  • Mission-Critical Work: We don't build for "what if." We build systems the Department of War actively needs to counter immediate, real-world threats.

  • The Builder's Playground: Work in a brand-new lab fully optimized for rapid prototyping, equipped with NVIDIA Jetsons, high-end scopes, and 3-D printers.

  • 100% Employer-Paid Premiums: We cover 100% of your medical, dental, and vision insurance premiums and cover 50% of healthcare premiums for your dependents.

  • Unlimited PTO: We value results, not clock-watching. Take the time you need to stay sharp and recharge.

  • Zero Red Tape: You have the autonomy to make technical decisions that would take months of committee approval at a larger firm.

  • Austin-Based Culture: Join an onsite team in Austin, TX, where we prioritize high-bandwidth collaboration and rapid field-testing.

  • Relocation Assistance: We want the best talent in the room. If you aren't in Austin yet, we’ll help you get here, to make your transition to the Silicon Hills seamless.

About the Interview

  1. Initial Screening with recruiter - 30 min phone call

  2. 1st Round Virtual Interview - peer engineer + SWE Director (45 min via MS Teams)

  3. 2nd Round Onsite Interview - CTO + Director + VP + peer(s) (~ 6 hours in-person) **will fly out candidates that are not local

  4. Reference checks & offer

9 Mothers Policy on the Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) During the Interview Process

The interviewing process is a mutual opportunity for us to get to know each other better. Our goal is to understand your unique background, evaluate your problem-solving abilities, and ensure a strong mutual fit.

AI is a core part of how we work at 9 Mothers—we actively encourage and frequently leverage AI tools in our day-to-day operations. However, during the hiring process, we need to evaluate your fundamental skills and expertise, not the outputs of an AI model.

To ensure a fair and transparent process, we ask that you adhere to the following interview guidelines:

  • 1st-Round Interviews (No AI Allowed): The use of AI tools, assistants, code generation tools, or real-time copilots is strictly prohibited during all first-round interviews and assessments. The use of AI during this stage will result in immediate disqualification from the hiring process.

  • 2nd-Round Interviews (Guided AI Usage): The second-round process includes opportunities to utilize AI. Your interview team will provide explicit guidance on how, when, and which AI tools to leverage during this stage.

We appreciate your cooperation in helping us maintain an authentic and fair interview experience for everyone.

About 9 Mothers

While others build for "awareness" or "long-term research," we build for the immediate survival of those in harm’s way. We are a team of hackers, engineers, and mission-driven builders who value field-ready capability over polished slide decks. If you want to see your code or hardware in the field next month—not next year—this is your playground.

Position Summary

EDDA is only as good as its actuators, and we're hiring the person who owns them. You will be our servo wizard: the single owner of every motor, actuator, gearbox and solenoid in the product, from the first torque and inertia calculation through supplier selection, bench characterization, control-loop tuning, abuse testing and production release. You are as fluent in gearbox design — backlash, torsional stiffness, efficiency, lubrication, lifetime — as you are inside the current loop of the servo driving it. And you have lived with motion systems that get rained on, dropped, fired next to and bounced across a field on the back of a truck.

What You'll Own

Everything in the product that converts electrons into motion is yours — the parts, the suppliers, the test data and the tuning.

  • Motors and actuators: BLDC/PMSM and frameless torque motors, steppers where they earn their place, linear actuators — every axis that moves EDDA's azimuth, elevation and auxiliary mechanisms.

  • Gearboxes and drivetrain: planetary, strain-wave (harmonic), cycloidal, worm and belt stages; the direct-drive-versus-geared call on each axis; bearing arrangements, preload, backlash and the stiffness budget that sets achievable control bandwidth.

  • Solenoids and discrete actuators: latches, safeties, indexing and release mechanisms — the fast, simple actuators that must work every time, in the cold, after being dropped.

  • Motor drives and tuning: drive selection or specification, commutation and feedback (encoders, resolvers, Hall sensors), current/velocity/position loop tuning, feedforward and filtering.

  • Characterization and test: dynamometer and bench rigs, thermal derating, torque ripple and cogging, efficiency maps, endurance and abuse testing, and the acceptance tests production runs on every unit.

  • The actuation supply chain: vendor qualification, custom motor and gearbox specifications, second sources, cost-down and the lead times that production depends on.

Essential Duties

  • Size and select: turn slew-rate, acceleration, pointing-accuracy and duty-cycle requirements into torque, speed, reflected-inertia and thermal budgets; pick or specify the motor, gear ratio and drive that meet them with margin — and show the math.

  • Design the drivetrain: own the mechanical path from rotor to load — gear stages, couplings, shafts, bearings, preload, lubrication and seals — and the stiffness and backlash budget that determines how hard the loops can be pushed.

  • Characterize everything: build the rigs and run the tests — torque constant, back-EMF, inductance, cogging and ripple, friction and stiction, efficiency, thermal rise, backlash and lost motion — so tuning starts from a measured plant, not a datasheet.

  • Tune the loops: commission and tune current, velocity and position loops (PID, feedforward, notch filters, observers) for aggressive high-bandwidth tracking without exciting structural modes or cooking the motor.

  • Engineer for abuse: design and qualify actuation for shock and vibration from vehicle mounts and weapon firing, dust, mud, water, salt, EMI and temperature extremes; lead failure analysis when hardware comes back from the range broken, and make sure the next revision doesn't.

  • Own the supply chain: qualify vendors, write motor, gearbox and solenoid specifications, manage second sources and lead times, and drive cost-down for production volumes.

  • Bridge the teams: be the technical interface between mechanical, electrical, firmware and robotics on anything that moves; triage failures at the hardware-software boundary and call whether a problem is mechanical, electrical or control.

  • Document and release: derating curves, tuning procedures, acceptance tests and drawings that production and field teams can execute without you in the room.

Requirements

  • Experience: 10+ years in mechatronics or motion-system engineering with a track record of shipping servo-driven products — ideally pan-tilt units, gimbals, turrets, robotic joints or vehicle-mounted systems.

  • Servo depth: hands-on selection, commissioning and tuning of BLDC/PMSM servo systems: field-oriented control, current/velocity/position loops, encoder and resolver feedback, drive configuration, and diagnosing instability, resonance and thermal limits on the bench.

  • Gearbox fluency: working command of planetary, strain-wave, cycloidal and worm drives — ratio selection, efficiency, backlash, torsional stiffness, lubrication and lifetime — and a clear sense of when direct drive beats gearing.

  • Actuator characterization: you have built test rigs and run dynamometer, thermal, efficiency and endurance tests; comfortable with scopes, current probes, DAQ and Python or MATLAB to extract plant parameters from data.

  • Drivetrain design: can design and detail the mechanical path from rotor to load — bearings, shafts, couplings, seals, preload — in CAD (SolidWorks or similar) with tolerance analysis.

  • Programming: enough C/C++ or Python to configure drives, automate tests and prototype control code; comfortable reading motor-control firmware.

  • Supplier management: have specified custom motors or gearboxes with vendors and run qualification, second-sourcing and cost-down.

  • Hands-on rigor: you build, break, measure and fix your own hardware.

  • Compliance: U.S. citizenship and the ability to pass a background check.

Nice‑to‑Have

  • Harsh-environment qualification: MIL-STD-810 shock and vibration, IP-rated sealing, EMI/EMC, thermal cycling — and the scars from hardware that was abused in the field anyway.

  • Weapon-mounted, recoil-loaded or vehicle-mounted motion systems.

  • Custom motor design: frameless, outer-rotor or slotless motors and magnetics; electromagnetic FEA (Ansys Maxwell, JMAG, FEMM).

  • Solenoid and voice-coil design: force-stroke-thermal trade-offs, PWM hold, fast actuation.

  • Structural dynamics: modal analysis and designing control around structural modes; stabilization on a moving platform.

  • Advanced control: model-predictive, adaptive or disturbance-observer control.

  • Drive ecosystems: CAN, EtherCAT, ROS 2/DDS; hands-on time with ODrive, moteus, Elmo, Copley, Kollmorgen or similar drives.

  • Production experience: DFM, incoming inspection and acceptance-test procedures for actuators.

  • Security clearance or the ability to obtain one.

  • You build robots, race drones or rebuild machinery on your own time.

Benefits

  • Meaningful Early Equity: You aren't just an employee; you are a foundational owner. Your contributions directly drive the value of your stake in the company.

  • Direct Roadmap Influence: Forget the bureaucracy of big defense. You will have a seat at the table, directly shaping our product and technology trajectory from day one.

  • Mission-Critical Work: We don't build for "what if." We build systems the Department of War actively needs to counter immediate, real-world threats.

  • The Builder's Playground: Work in a brand-new lab fully optimized for rapid prototyping, equipped with NVIDIA Jetsons, high-end scopes, and 3-D printers.

  • 100% Employer-Paid Premiums: We cover 100% of your medical, dental, and vision insurance premiums and cover 50% of healthcare premiums for your dependents.

  • Unlimited PTO: We value results, not clock-watching. Take the time you need to stay sharp and recharge.

  • Zero Red Tape: You report to the founders. You have the autonomy to make technical decisions that would take months of committee approval at a larger firm.

  • Austin-Based Culture: Join an onsite team in Austin, TX, where we prioritize high-bandwidth collaboration and rapid field-testing.

  • Relocation Assistance: We want the best talent in the room. If you aren't in Austin yet, we’ll help you get here, to make your transition to the Silicon Hills seamless.

  1. Virtual interview (45 min via MS Teams)

  2. Onsite interview in Austin (1.5 hr in-person)

Employment Type: Direct Hire, Full-Time

Job Title: Radar Engineer

About 9 Mothers

The modern battlefield has changed. Cheap, autonomous suicide drones have turned the tactical advantage upside down, and the world is looking for a solution. At 9 Mothers, we aren’t just "innovating"—we are building the shield.

Backed by top-tier investors, we develop AI powered machines designed to intercept and neutralize Group 1/sUAS threats in real-time. Our flagship product is a low-power, counter-drone system built for the edge—on vehicles, at bases, or in a soldier's pack.

While others build for "awareness" or "long-term research," we build for the immediate survival of those in harm’s way. We are a team of hackers, engineers, and mission-driven builders who value field-ready capability over polished slide decks. If you want to see your code or hardware in the field next month—not next year—this is your playground.

Position Summary

9 Mothers is hiring a Radar Engineer to own the radar sensing layer of our counter-sUAS kill chain. In this role, you will integrate and tune radars from multiple vendors so that their detections and tracks feed cleanly into our platform—alongside our passive acoustic (Vor) and in-house visual detection stack—giving Edda and future systems an earlier, more reliable picture of incoming threats.

You will own the full radar lifecycle: characterizing sensors, writing the software that ingests and processes radar data, tuning radar configurations for performance against small, fast, low-RCS targets in cluttered environments, and validating that performance on the range. This role sits at the intersection of RF engineering, embedded and real-time software, and systems integration in a fast-moving defense startup environment.

Essential Duties

Radar Characterization: Run bench and range characterization of the

 
 

radars we field (e.g., FMCW, pulse-Doppler, electronically scanned arrays) to verify vendor performance claims and establish baselines for tuning.

Radar Integration: Integrate multiple radar models into our counter-drone platform, including mechanical/electrical interfaces, timing and synchronization, coordinate-frame alignment, and vendor SDKs, APIs, and data protocols.

Software Development: Design, build, and maintain the software that configures radars and ingests, filters, and publishes their detections and tracks to the rest of our system in a reliable, low-latency manner.

Performance Tuning: Tune radar parameters—waveform and mode selection, detection thresholds, CFAR, clutter maps, Doppler filtering, and track initiation/maintenance—to maximize probability of detection and minimize false alarms against small, fast sUAS in real-world environments.

Sensor Fusion Support: Work with the perception and controls teams to fuse radar tracks with acoustic and EO/IR data, and to cue our visual tracking and effectors from radar.

Testing & Validation: Build and execute test plans, including simulation, hardware-in-the-loop, and live-flight range testing with our UAS pilots, and establish metrics for detection range, track quality, latency, and false-alarm rate.

Field & Customer Support: Support radar setup, site surveys, and tuning during customer demonstrations, pilots, and field deployments, troubleshooting issues from the RF front end through the software stack.

Documentation: Produce and maintain integration documentation, interface control documents (ICDs), tuning guides, and test reports for internal teams and external partners.

Requirements

Radar Experience: 5+ years of hands-on experience as a radar engineer, radar systems engineer, or similar role, including work with more than one radar type or vendor.

Job Title: Senior Robotics Engineer

 

Company Overview

9 Mothers Defense develops AI-enabled systems to counter unmanned aerial threats. Our first product, EDDA, is an autonomous counter-sUAS point-defense platform designed to detect, track, and neutralize Group 1 drone threats. The company is headquartered in Austin, Texas.

 

Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced Robotics Software Engineer to join a small, fast‑moving team. You will design and implement the physical software control systems — the “body” — of our interceptor platforms. This role is critical, as the accuracy of our control theory dictates the success of every high‑speed maneuver in combat. You should be comfortable writing code and working with robotic components (actuators, controllers, compute, sensors, etc.).

 

Essential Duties

  • Design and implement high‑bandwidth software control loops and advanced control algorithms (e.g., PID control) to ensure vehicle stability and enable high‑speed, precise maneuvers under dynamic load.

  • Write high‑quality, efficient code (primarily Rust, C, or C++) to control and manage actuators, motor drivers (via CAN bus), and sensors on a real‑time operating system (RTOS).

  • Integrate and fuse sensor data from cameras and IMUs (using methods such as EKF/UKF) on embedded systems (e.g., NVIDIA Jetson) to achieve reliable, real‑time state estimation.

  • Act as the final link in the autonomy chain, translating tracking output from the computer vision system into reliable motor commands that accurately steer the interceptor.

  • Define, build, and maintain Python tools for calibration, logging, and CI/CD, ensuring rapid iteration and deployment.

 

Requirements

  • Control theory & embedded systems: Strong grasp of PID control, motor drivers, CAN bus, and RTOS fundamentals. Expertise in designing control and performance for robotics applications.

  • Programming/frameworks: Hands‑on experience building embedded robotics systems. Proficiency in Rust, C, or C++ for speed and direct hardware interaction.

  • Hardware: Experience with embedded platforms such as NVIDIA Jetson and camera pipelines. Skilled in managing scopes, logic/CAN analyzers, and basic rework.

  • U.S. Citizenship and the ability to pass a background check

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with ROS2, DDS, or similar middleware

  • Model‑predictive or adaptive control expertise

  • PCB design and EMC awareness

  • Safety‑critical workflow experience

  • Prior defense startup experience

  • Security clearance or ability to obtain one

  • Passion for building robots or engineering projects as a hobby

 

Benefits

  • Meaningful Early Equity: You aren't just an employee; you are a foundational owner. Your contributions directly drive the value of your stake in the company.

  • Direct Roadmap Influence: Forget the bureaucracy of big defense. You will have a seat at the table, directly shaping our product and technology trajectory from day one.

  • Mission-Critical Work: We don't build for "what if." We build systems the Department of War actively needs to counter immediate, real-world threats.

  • The Builder's Playground: Work in a brand-new lab fully optimized for rapid prototyping, equipped with NVIDIA Jetsons, high-end scopes, and 3-D printers.

  • 100% Employer-Paid Premiums: We cover 100% of your medical, dental, and vision insurance premiums and cover 50% of healthcare premiums for your dependents.

  • Unlimited PTO: We value results, not clock-watching. Take the time you need to stay sharp and recharge.

  • Zero Red Tape: You report to the founders. You have the autonomy to make technical decisions that would take months of committee approval at a larger firm.

  • Austin-Based Culture: Join an onsite team in Austin, TX, where we prioritize high-bandwidth collaboration and rapid field-testing.

  • Relocation Assistance: We want the best talent in the room. If you aren't in Austin yet, we’ll help you get here, to make your transition to the Silicon Hills seamless.

 

About the Interview

  1. Initial Screening with recruiter - 30 min phone call

  2. 1st Round Virtual Interview - Peer Engineer + senior leader (45 min via MS Teams)

  3. 2nd Round Onsite Interview - CTO + Director + VP + peer(s) (~ 6 hours in-person) **will fly out candidates that are not local

  4. Reference checks & offer

9 Mothers Policy on the Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) During the Interview Process

The interviewing process is a mutual opportunity for us to get to know each other better. Our goal is to understand your unique background, evaluate your problem-solving abilities, and ensure a strong mutual fit.

AI is a core part of how we work at 9 Mothers—we actively encourage and frequently leverage AI tools in our day-to-day operations. However, during the hiring process, we need to evaluate your fundamental skills and expertise, not the outputs of an AI model.

To ensure a fair and transparent process, we ask that you adhere to the following interview guidelines:

  • 1st-Round Interviews (No AI Allowed): The use of AI tools, assistants, code generation tools, or real-time copilots is strictly prohibited during all first-round interviews and assessments. The use of AI during this stage will result in immediate disqualification from the hiring process.

  • 2nd-Round Interviews (Guided AI Usage): The second-round process includes opportunities to utilize AI. Your interview team will provide explicit guidance on how, when, and which AI tools to leverage during this stage.

We appreciate your cooperation in helping us maintain an authentic and fair interview experience for everyone.

MIL-spec circular connectors and continuous-flex cable where a harness crosses the elevation axis and takes recoil; a less-rugged sealed connector and standard jacket where it sits bolted inside the base. You defend each call with test data and a cost roll-up.

  • Power: battery, bus and motor-drive feeds — conductor sizing, voltage drop, thermal budgets, fusing, grounding.

  • Signal and data: encoder, sensor, CAN, Ethernet, USB and camera links, with the shielding they need.

  • Fiber and hybrid: EMI-immune, high-bandwidth links between sensor heads and compute, including copper/fiber hybrids through one rugged connector.

  • Moving axes: continuous-flex and torsion-rated cables, service loops, cable carriers and slip-ring interfaces across EDDA's azimuth and elevation joints.

  • Source and release: qualify contract manufacturers, run RFQs, manage second sources and lead times, and release drawings and acceptance tests that production can build from without you.

  • Workmanship: IPC/WHMA-A-620 fluent; you crimp with calibrated tooling and pull-test your terminations.
